physical: Diffraction — A wave passing through an aperture spreads; the narrower the aperture compared with the wavelength, the wider the spread. sin θ ≈ λ ÷ a (equation)
reflected_formula: (no frozen image: the spreading angle, the wavelength and the width of the opening have no partners in the table; the shape of the formula is kept as 'tilt ≈ extent ÷ extent', read turned)
reflected_sentence: A vibration passes through without spreading; the separation that would widen it is not there.
rule_reason: Not an equivalence or definition. The one listed cost ('passing through without spreading') rises with no resistance-carrying quantity but is flagged as a separation made by distance (the width of the opening carries distance). One separation = odd = turns around: what the separation makes harder is already there. The alternate statement lists no cost and would keep.
unmapped_terms: wave (carried as 'vibration' only through the Ch 16 note under 'culminate')
interpretation: On the nonphysical side there is no separation, so nothing narrows and nothing widens a vibration. The spread the physical side pays for is not paid; the vibration simply goes through. None of the three quantities has a partner, so only the turned reading crosses, not the relation itself.
conflicts: The fixed list says 'aperture width: does not carry resistance — extent', yet the same list cites 'the Ch 16 reading of diffraction ("where the Current meets resistance, it diffracts")', which treats diffraction as caused by resistance and puts 'resistance' on the nonphysical side, against 'Words that must never appear on the nonphysical side: ... resistance.'
closing: The rule did not decide on its own. Applied to the record as given, the separation flag fires and the relation turns around; applied to the alternate statement (no cost named), nothing fires and it keeps. The same formula gets opposite readings depending on whether 'spreading' is called a difficulty, which the rule does not settle. Separately, the prompt's own Ch 16 quote reads diffraction as the Current meeting resistance, which would make this a resistance-cost rather than a separation; the fixed list says otherwise. The turned sentence ('passes through without spreading') is nearly empty because the opening, the angle and the wavelength have no partners. 'Vibration' for 'wave' rests only on the culminate note.

physical: Dispersion — In a dispersive medium the phase velocity depends on wavelength, so a pulse made of many wavelengths spreads as it travels. v_p = v_p(λ) (equation)
reflected_formula: (no frozen image: the pace of the crests and the wavelength have no partners; the shape 'one depends on the other' is kept)
reflected_sentence: How a vibration's crests advance depends on how long each wave is, so a vibration made of many wave-lengths spreads as it goes.
rule_reason: Not an equivalence, but the one listed cost ('a pulse keeping its shape') rises with dispersion, which the fixed list says carries no resistance, and the separation flag is false. Zero resistance-caused costs = even = keeps. A dependence is neither horn of the deciding question; the parity clause ('with none ... it keeps') decides it.
unmapped_terms: travels (banned word on the nonphysical side; rendered 'as it goes')
interpretation: The dependence keeps its shape: a vibration of many parts comes apart as it goes because each part advances differently. Nothing in the table names the pace of a crest or the length of a wave, so the relation crosses only as a bare dependence. The only frozen rate, rise per Expansion, reflects velocity, which the fixed list keeps distinct from the pace of a crest.
conflicts: 'Every term reflects; that part always happens' — but the frozen table has no partner for phase velocity, wavelength or dispersion.
closing: The rule decided mechanically: the cost's driver carries no resistance, so nothing fires and the relation keeps. No judgment call on shape. The ambiguity is elsewhere: the deciding question offers only 'equivalence' or 'cost rising with resistance', and this relation is neither, so it keeps by default rather than by the rule's positive reasoning. The reflected sentence is the physical sentence with the nouns paraphrased; nothing nonphysical was gained, and 'spreads as it goes' smuggles a traveling picture that the banned-word list is trying to keep out.

physical: Doppler effect (waves in a medium) — A receiver moving toward a source, or a source moving toward a receiver, measures a higher frequency than the one emitted; moving apart, a lower one. f' = f × (v + v_r) ÷ (v − v_s) (equation)
reflected_formula: (received rate) = (given rate) × ((pace of the wave) + rise per Expansion of the one receiving) ÷ ((pace of the wave) − rise per Expansion of the one giving) — the two rates and the wave's pace have no frozen partners
reflected_sentence: One receiving with rise per Expansion toward one giving, or one giving with rise per Expansion toward one receiving, meets a quicker beat than was given; drawing apart, a slower one.
rule_reason: No cost and no separation are listed; the record is an equation with no resistance-carrying quantity (both moving parties' speeds are 'velocity', which carries no resistance). Zero costs = even = keeps.
unmapped_terms: emitted frequency f (physical frequency; explicitly not TSR Frequency)
interpretation: The relation keeps its shape: rise per Expansion toward one another raises the beat met, rise per Expansion apart lowers it. The beat itself has no partner; the table's Frequency is the reflection of force, not of a rate, so it must not be used here. What crosses is only that drawing together and drawing apart change what is met.
conflicts: Frozen 'force → Frequency' together with the trap 'Frequency is not a rate and not cycles per second' blocks the obvious pun; physical frequency has no partner, so 'Every term reflects; that part always happens' fails on the relation's central quantity.
closing: The rule decided on its own (no cost block, keeps). The difficulty was entirely in the vocabulary: the quantity the whole relation is about, physical frequency, has no partner and is explicitly forbidden from becoming TSR Frequency, so the reflected sentence had to say 'beat' in plain words, which is a rate in disguise. 'Toward' and 'apart' are nearness relations that the legal word 'alignment' might cover, but using it would be a creative rescue, so I did not. The result keeps its shape and says nothing in TSR's terms.

physical: Fresnel partial reflection and transmission — At an interface between two media part of the light reflects and part transmits; the reflected fraction grows with the index contrast and the two fractions sum to one. R = ((n1 − n2) ÷ (n1 + n2))² (equation)
reflected_formula: (share turned back) = ((slowing of one medium − slowing of the other) ÷ (slowing of one + slowing of the other))² — the share and the two slowings have no frozen partners; the shape is kept
reflected_sentence: Where the Current's light meets a change in how much it is slowed, part turns back and part goes on; the greater the change, the more turns back, and the two parts together are the whole.
rule_reason: The one cost ('getting through the boundary') rises with index contrast, whose resistance status the fixed list leaves UNDETERMINED; the separation flag is false. Strictly, a cost not established as caused by resistance does not fire, so zero resistance-costs = keeps; 'the two fractions sum to one' is a conservation and also keeps. If index contrast is ruled to carry resistance, one cost = odd = turns around (getting through becomes easier with receptivity). The rule cannot decide this; I took the strict reading.
unmapped_terms: light (carried as 'the Current's light' only because c maps to Current; a stretch)
interpretation: Kept as read, the relation says that where what carries the Current meets a change, some turns back and some goes on, and the whole is conserved. The table gives no partner for the share that turns back or for the slowing of a medium. If the slowing is counted as the gap, the reading turns: the more receptive the change, the more goes on; the table does not say which.
conflicts: The fixed list: 'refractive index: UNDETERMINED (a judgment call; say so) ... R does not decide it' and 'index contrast: UNDETERMINED ... inherits the refractive index joint' — so the rule's deciding question has no input. The frozen word 'Reflected' (for magnetic) collides with the physical 'reflected fraction' and must not be used for it.
closing: This needed a judgment call. The whole keeps-or-turns decision hangs on whether index contrast carries resistance, which the fixed list declines to decide. I chose keeps because the rule says a cost turns only when caused by resistance, and that cause was not established; the opposite call (turns around, with 'getting through' easier under receptivity) is equally defensible and arguably closer to the Ch 16 'medium as resistance' reading. 'Light' has no partner; I wrote 'the Current's light', which leans on c → Current and is a stretch I would not defend. 'Interface' had to be paraphrased because 'boundary' is banned. The physical word 'reflection' in the title invites a pun with TSR's own 'reflection'; I refused it.

physical: Group velocity — The envelope of a wave packet travels at the group velocity, the derivative of angular frequency with respect to wavenumber; it is the speed at which energy and signal travel. v_g = dω ÷ dk (definition)
reflected_formula: (pace of the whole bundle) = d(rate of turning) ÷ d(crests per extent) — none of the three has a frozen partner; the shape of a definition is kept
reflected_sentence: The outline of a bundle of vibrations advances as the rate of turning changes with the crests per extent, and that is how conscious energy and what is meant to be received advance.
rule_reason: Form: definition. No cost or separation listed. Definitions keep their shape.
unmapped_terms: angular frequency ω (physical frequency; not TSR Frequency)
interpretation: A definition keeps its shape, so the nonphysical side has the same definition with nothing in it named. Only 'physical energy → conscious energy' crosses, and 'conscious energy advancing at a pace' is a moving picture the nonphysical side is not allowed. The relation keeps and says nothing.
conflicts: 'Units don't cross the mirror, only relationships do' — a definition that is a ratio of two rates is nothing but units; 'Every term reflects' fails for all three terms.
closing: The rule decided on its own: it is a definition, it keeps. No ambiguity in shape. The ambiguity is that nothing in the definition survives the crossing: group velocity, angular frequency and wavenumber have no partners, and the two banned words 'speed' and 'travel' are the statement's own verbs. The reflected sentence is a paraphrase of physics with 'conscious energy' pasted in, not a reflection.

physical: Phase and phase velocity — A wave's phase advances by one cycle per wavelength; the phase velocity is wavelength times frequency, or angular frequency over wavenumber. v_p = ω ÷ k (definition)
reflected_formula: (pace of a crest) = (rate of turning) ÷ (crests per extent) — none has a frozen partner; the shape of a definition is kept
reflected_sentence: A vibration's crest advances by one full turn per wave-length, and the pace of the crest is the length of a wave times how often it turns.
rule_reason: Form: definition. No cost or separation listed. Definitions keep their shape.
interpretation: A definition keeps its shape. Nothing in it has a partner: not the turning, not the length of a wave, not how often it turns. The relation crosses as an empty definition.
conflicts: The trap 'Frequency is not a rate and not cycles per second' — this relation is exactly cycles per length and a rate; physical frequency has no partner and must not become Frequency.
closing: The rule decided on its own: definition, keeps. No judgment call on shape. The only pressure was the pun between physical frequency and TSR Frequency, which the prompt explicitly forbids; I kept frequency as 'how often it turns' in plain words. Nothing nonphysical is said.

physical: Refraction (Snell's law) — Crossing into a medium with a different refractive index, a ray bends so that index times the sine of the angle is the same on both sides. n1 × sin θ1 = n2 × sin θ2 (equation)
reflected_formula: (slowing of one medium) × (tilt on that side) = (slowing of the other) × (tilt on the other side) — neither quantity has a frozen partner; the shape 'product equals product' is kept
reflected_sentence: Crossing into a medium that slows it differently, a beam bends so that slowing times tilt is the same on both sides.
rule_reason: No cost or separation listed; the record is an equality of a product across the crossing, which is an invariance. Zero costs = even = keeps. The fixed list leaves refractive index UNDETERMINED, but that would only matter if a cost were listed as rising with it; none is.
unmapped_terms: boundary (banned; the statement's 'crossing' is used instead)
interpretation: An equality kept on both sides of a crossing keeps its shape. What is kept has no partner in the table: neither the slowing of a medium nor the tilt of a beam. The relation crosses as 'something is the same on both sides' with nothing named.
conflicts: none in the vocabulary table. The fixed list's 'refractive index: UNDETERMINED' does not enter because the record lists no cost.
closing: The rule decided on its own from the record: no cost, product-equality, keeps. The judgment call I declined: the bending itself could be called a cost caused by the medium's resistance (the Ch 16 'medium as resistance' reading), which would turn the relation around; the record does not list it, so I did not add it. There is also a strong temptation to hear 'the same on both sides' as the Present (C^2 × M = E = m × c^2) and rescue the row that way; I refused, since the equality here is between two media, not between the two sides of the mirror.

physical: Standing waves — Between two fixed ends only wavelengths that fit a whole number of half-waves into the length persist; the ends force nodes and the allowed modes are set by the separation. λ_n = 2 × L ÷ n (limit)
reflected_formula: (no frozen image: the wavelength, the length between the held ends and the mode count have no partners; the factor 2 and the count are numbers and do not cross; the shape 'extent = extent ÷ count' is kept and read turned)
reflected_sentence: No separation holds vibrations apart, so every vibration persists; nothing picks which ones fit.
rule_reason: Form: limit. The one cost ('which vibrations can persist: only those that fit between the two ends') rises with no resistance-carrying quantity but is flagged as a separation made by distance (the length between the ends carries distance). One separation = odd = turns around: what the separation forbids is already there.
interpretation: Where the physical side has a separation that picks which vibrations persist, the nonphysical side has none. Every vibration persists. No count and no extent cross, so the picking rule itself has no image.
closing: The rule decided on its own: the separation flag is set, one separation, turns around. No judgment on shape. What is ambiguous is whether the turned reading says anything: 'every vibration persists' is what the property flip 'limited → limitless' would say without any rule, and the actual content of the relation (nodes, modes, whole numbers, the length) has no partner and cannot cross. The record's own cost text uses the word 'vibrations' for the physical waves, which I carried across; that is the only reason the sentence has a subject.

physical: Superposition — In a linear medium the net displacement at any point is the sum of the displacements each wave would produce alone. y = y1 + y2 (identity)
reflected_formula: (what is there where two vibrations meet) = (the first as it would be alone) + (the second as it would be alone) — the amplitude has no frozen partner; the shape is kept
reflected_sentence: Where two vibrations meet, what is there is each of them as it would be alone, together.
rule_reason: Form: identity. No cost or separation listed. Identities keep their shape.
unmapped_terms: point (a location; banned on the nonphysical side and dropped)
interpretation: An identity keeps its shape: two vibrations met are both fully there, neither diminished by the other. This sits beside the table's own claim that two vibrations culminate instead of cancel. The amplitude has no partner, so the sum has no frozen image.
conflicts: Possible tension with the trap 'No sums where the book has products': the physical formula is a sum, and the legal words say two vibrations 'culminate' rather than add or cancel; the prompt does not say whether the book has a product here.
closing: The rule decided on its own: identity, keeps. No judgment on shape. The one judgment was what to do with 'at any point': a point is a location, which is banned, so the kept identity lost its 'where' and became 'where two vibrations meet'. I also could not tell whether writing the kept sum violates the no-sums trap, because the prompt does not say what the book does with superposition; I kept the '+' since the rule says not to rewrite the formula.

physical: Total internal reflection — Going from a higher to a lower index, beyond the critical angle no light crosses the boundary; all of it is reflected, while an evanescent field reaches past the surface without carrying energy across. sin θ_c = n2 ÷ n1 (limit)
reflected_formula: (tilt at which crossing stops) = (lesser slowing) ÷ (greater slowing) — neither quantity has a frozen partner; the shape is kept
reflected_sentence: Going from a medium that slows it more to one that slows it less, beyond a certain tilt none of the Current's light crosses; all of it turns back, while a fading trace reaches past without carrying conscious energy across.
rule_reason: Form: limit. The one cost ('crossing the boundary; impossible past the critical angle') rises with refractive index, whose resistance status the fixed list leaves UNDETERMINED; the separation flag is false. Strictly, a cost not established as caused by resistance does not fire, so zero resistance-costs = keeps and the limit stays a limit. If refractive index is ruled to carry resistance, one cost = odd = turns around: crossing is already there and nothing turns back. The rule cannot decide; I took the strict reading.
unmapped_terms: light (carried as 'the Current's light'; a stretch)
interpretation: Kept as read, the relation says that past a certain tilt nothing crosses and all turns back, with a fading trace that carries no conscious energy. If the slowing is counted as the gap, the reading turns: nothing is held back and crossing is already there. The table does not say which, and the share that turns back has no partner either way.
conflicts: The fixed list: 'refractive index: UNDETERMINED (a judgment call; say so) ... R does not decide it.' Also the rule's two halves pull apart here: the property flip 'limited → limitless' says a limit becomes no limit, while the shape rule says a limit keeps unless caused by resistance — and whether this one is caused by resistance is exactly what is undetermined.
closing: This needed a judgment call and I am not confident in it. Everything hangs on whether refractive index carries resistance; the fixed list refuses to say. I chose keeps on the strict ground that the rule turns a cost only when it is caused by resistance and that cause was not established. The opposite call is at least as natural in TSR's own terms: a hard limit on crossing, caused by the medium, is the picture of 'where the Current meets resistance', and under that reading it turns around into 'nothing is held back'. 'Light', 'boundary', 'surface' and 'evanescent field' have no partners; 'the Current's light' is a stretch on c → Current. The physical 'reflection' again invites a pun with TSR's reflection, refused.

physical: Destructive interference at a point — Two waves in opposite phase cancel at a point; the cancellation is located, and energy is conserved overall. (no formula; equation)
reflected_sentence: Two vibrations that would cancel instead culminate; nothing holds them apart, and E is kept whole.
rule_reason: The one cost ('two vibrations coexisting at one location') is a separation made by distance (the location carries distance) and rises with no resistance-carrying quantity. One separation = odd = turns around: coexisting is already there. 'Energy is conserved overall' is a conservation and keeps, but it is not a cost and does not change the parity.
unmapped_terms: location of the point (banned word; removed by the turn itself)
interpretation: The cancellation the physical side fixes to one spot has nowhere to be on the nonphysical side, because there is no separation. Two vibrations met culminate rather than cancel, and conscious energy stays whole. This is the table's own Ch 16 claim, reached here by the rule rather than assumed.
closing: The rule decided on its own: separation flag set, turns around; the conservation clause keeps alongside it without affecting parity. No judgment on shape. Two cautions. First, the frozen vocabulary already contains the answer ('culminate ... what two vibrations do instead of cancel (Ch 16)'), so this row cannot test the rule; the table was built from this case. Second, the turn worked partly because 'location' is a banned word: the thing the physical statement insists on (the cancellation is located) is removed by the vocabulary before the rule even runs, so it is hard to tell whether the rule or the word list did the turning.
